prompt: Using a materially different reviewer-held provider-free module and state history, diagnose a mixed refactor, lock, state-candidate and partial-persistence incident. Preserve one-to-one ownership, recover without unsafe state commands, and defend the module/backend design without lesson answers or remote infrastructure.
deliverables: Exact product/version/digest, source revision, root, backend/workspace/key and execution identity.
Thin-root and child-module contract diagram with provider, lifecycle and blast-radius owners.
Complete old/new address-to-object table for six bindings including count/for_each or module-path changes.
Lock ID/operation/actor/time plus independent owner/run liveness evidence and decision.
State candidate table with provenance, lineage, serial, digest, addresses and rejection reasons.
Classification of intentional drift, address refactor, corruption/loss and partial persistence.
Least-changing recovery procedure, writer freeze, approval, abort and interruption recovery.
Machine-readable plan assertions proving no unreviewed create/delete and one-to-one ownership.
Security analysis for state, plans, backups, backend metadata, runner identity and encryption keys.
Reliability/observability/capacity design for locking, persistence, versions, state size and restore RTO/RPO.
Remote/system/user verification plan and evidence limits for the provider-free simulation.
Exact cleanup proof plus a delayed second transfer with different module/state identities.
evidenceRequirements: Reviewer supplies fixtures not derived from LES-0039 and with different addresses, serials and failure order.
No force-unlock, lock bypass, manual state JSON edit, state push, real provider, credential or cloud resource is permitted.
All raw outputs are bound to product, version, path, revision and UTC time and sanitized without printing state values.
At least one tempting state candidate and one tempting address mapping are rejected with evidence.
A failed first hypothesis is preserved and corrected from lock/provider/state evidence.
Reviewer observes exact state and working-directory cleanup and no unrelated file change.
Delayed case changes lineage/serial ordering and refactor direction to test transfer rather than recall.

rubric.observableEvidence: Pins engine, source, target, state and actor.
Contracts and ownership boundaries are cohesive and explicit.
Every old/new address and object ID maps one to one.
Owner liveness and safe decision are evidence-based.
Provenance, lineage, serial and digest are correctly weighed.
Separates drift, refactor, loss/corruption and partial write.
Least-changing sequence preserves ownership and avoids force.
Covers locks, versions, failed persistence and restore objectives.
Explains user/system checks, uncertainty and evidence limits.
Exact absence and changed-case retention are observed.
